newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vobis nine-month sales rise seven percent.
newsitem.headline: Vobis nine-month sales rise seven percent.

text.p: German computer retailer Vobis Microcomputer AG said on Wednesday the demise of some key competitors helped sales rise seven percent in the first nine months of 1996.

Pre-tax profit for all of 1996 is expected to rise one percent from the 1995 total of 50 million marks ($32.8 million), incoming chief executive Gert Huegler said in a statement. The company did not provide precise figures.
Vobis gained at the expense of archrival Escom Computer AG, which went bankrupt in July, said Huegler, who will succeed co-founder Theo Lieven as chief executive on January 1.
The difficulties faced by Compaq Computer Corp. and Apple Computer Inc. in the German retail market also eased the competitive pressure on Vobis, Huegler said.
"The U.S. firms do not rule with a free hand in Germany as they do elsewhere, thanks to Vobis and its Highscreen brand," Huegler said.
Extraordinary sales at Maxdata, a distributor owned by Vobis, also boosted the group's revenues, he said.
Vobis reported first-half sales rose five percent to 1.46 billion marks. In 1995, revenues were 3.085 billion marks.
Vobis is a unit of retailing concern Kaufhof AG. Siemens Nixdorf Informationssysteme AG also owns 10 percent of Vobis.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn newsroom, (49-228) 260 97 150 ($ = 1.525 German Marks)
